title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: THE REPORT'S OPEN-THE-PRIMARY RULE, APPLIED TO A TOOL INSTEAD OF A COMPANY, KILLED THE PREMISE OF STANDING ACTION (c): `/skill-doctor` REPORTS COST AND USAGE AND NOTHING ELSE, AND `claude plugin eval` — SHIPPED IN 2.1.269 OVERNIGHT — IS A PLUGIN AUTHOR'S TEST HARNESS, NOT AN AUDITOR YOU CAN POINT AT AN INSTALLED CORPUS
bullets.summary: Claude Code 2.1.269 (first seen Sep 11, after this morning's fire) added `claude plugin eval`: run a plugin's eval suite and get scored, reproducible results as JSON plus an HTML report. On its face that is standing action (c) shipped as a command, and this fire nearly filed it that way. Opening the reference instead produced the opposite finding. WHAT `plugin eval` ACTUALLY IS: each eval case is a prompt you write plus graders you write, run in a fresh throwaway workspace with a clean CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and HOME and ONLY THE PLUGIN UNDER TEST loaded, executed three times by default, optionally against a baseline arm without the plugin to report a delta; cases live in `evals/`, graders are typed (regex, tool_used, tool_order, file_exists, llm, baseline), output is `aggregate-result.json` plus `report.html`, exit codes distinguish pass, fail, partial-on-cost-ceiling, interrupted and terminated. It is early access, enabled per organization. It tests ONE plugin you are AUTHORING against tests you wrote. It cannot be aimed at ~130 installed skills and asked which ones are any good. WHAT `/skill-doctor` ACTUALLY IS: a per-skill usage and context-cost summary — tokens spent, 7-day invocation counts, never-invoked warnings, unused plugins flagged. That is the ECONOMY column and it is genuinely a command rather than a project. It reports nothing about PROVENANCE (where a skill came from, who wrote it, when upstream last moved) and nothing about QUALITY (whether an installed skill actually works). Source-quality note: the changelog is Anthropic's own CHANGELOG.md read through Releasebot's mirror, which links the raw primary; the `plugin eval` and `/skill-doctor` behavioural detail comes from the embedded Claude Code tool reference consulted directly this fire, and there is NO public documentation page for `plugin eval` yet, so the schema specifics should be re-confirmed against `claude plugin eval --help` on the actual machine before anyone builds against them.
bullets.how: YES, and it is a correction to this report, which is the most useful thing a second fire can produce. For four fires (c) has been written down as "the /skill-doctor economy audit across the ~130-skill corpus," and since Sep 11 as that audit plus a provenance column, with Sep 11's bullet 2 concluding the artifact was "build-or-buy, priced" because Anthropic had shipped smart reports and AIR had raised $50M. THAT CONCLUSION WAS WRONG IN ITS MOST IMPORTANT PART, and the error was the same one the aggregator rule was invented to stop — inheriting a capability claim from a description instead of opening the thing. Corrected framing, three columns, three different answers. ECONOMY: buyable, it is `/skill-doctor`, one command, and it is the column this report has been loudest about and it was never the hard one. PROVENANCE: NOT SOLD BY ANYONE in our stack — it is the twelve-repo path enumeration Sep 11 produced by accident plus a `git log -1` per repo, still a find command, still unwritten, and today's bullet 2 shows it has now been implicated twice in two days. QUALITY: not available as a product at all for an INSTALLED corpus; `plugin eval` would require authoring eval cases per skill, which for ~130 skills is a real project and should be scoped to the handful that actually run, which `/skill-doctor`'s 7-day counts would tell us. The operator consequence is that (c) stops being one overdue chore and becomes one cheap command, one cheap script, and one genuinely large thing we should NOT do for 130 skills. And note the enablement detail, which ties this bullet to the next one: clients running a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` do not get `plugin eval` automatically and need an enablement variable from Anthropic — so activating one of the profiles this morning's sweep found would silently cost us the tool.

bullets.title: CLAUDE CODE 2.1.268 FIXED EVERY TURN FAILING WITH HTTP 400 ON THIRD-PARTY ANTHROPIC-COMPATIBLE ENDPOINTS — WHICH IS THE BORING, CORRECT EXPLANATION FOR THIS MORNING'S MiniMax AND Z.ai FINDING, AND 2.1.269 SEPARATELY FIXED A PLUGIN-ARCHIVE PERMISSIONS CLASS ON THE EXACT ASSET STANDING ACTION (c) IS ABOUT
bullets.summary: Two items from the same changelog, both of which change how this morning's lead bullet should be read. FIRST, 2.1.268: "Fixed every turn failing with HTTP 400 on third-party Anthropic-compatible endpoints (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) since 2.1.265: a regex in the Artifact tool's input schema that those endpoints reject." Anthropic actively maintains compatibility with third-party Anthropic-shaped endpoints and treats breaking them as a regression worth a point release. That is the mundane, non-sinister reason a third-party settings repo ships `settings-minimax.json` and `settings-zai.json`: pointing Claude Code at an alternative backend is a SUPPORTED configuration, not a covert one. It does not change this morning's verdict — those two files remain PRESENT, NAMED, INERT — but it removes any temptation to read their existence as evidence of anything, and it is the correct note to have on the record before the threat-report framing hardens into folklore. SECOND, 2.1.269: "Fixed plugin archives extracted for a session being readable by other local users, extracted files keeping world-writable bits from the archive, and stale files surviving re-extraction." Also in the same release, a permission-bypass fix: `Edit()` deny rules and the write-path check did not apply to the file a Bash `tee` command writes, so a `Bash(tee:*)` allow rule could reach destinations outside the working directories. Source-quality note: vendor changelog, read as the primary; no CVE is attached to either item and Anthropic ships them as ordinary fixes rather than an advisory, so this is maintenance hygiene, not a disclosed exploit.
bullets.how: YES on the second item more than the first. A plugin archive whose extracted files keep world-writable bits, and whose stale files survive re-extraction, is a description of the ~130-skill corpus on Bobby's machine — the same corpus that standing action (c) is supposed to inventory, and the same one that Sep 11's GitSpawn sweep walked through twelve third-party repositories of. This is the SECOND time in two days that a routine vendor fix has landed on the skill corpus as an asset class, which is the actual argument for (c) that four fires of "it's overdue" never made: the corpus is not just an unmeasured cost, it is an unmeasured SURFACE, and it is the one part of the stack that grows by accretion from third parties. The action is the same one that was already free — update Claude Code, which takes the fixes, and run the provenance script from bullet 1, which is still a find command. The read on item one is narrower and is a correction to tone rather than substance: this report should not let a threat report make a supported configuration look like an incident. Inert is inert, and the reason it exists is documented in a changelog.

bullets.title: THE SAME RELEASE SHIPPED A CONCURRENT-AGENT FAN-OUT LEVER (1–256) AND A SUBAGENT MAP WITH PER-AGENT CARDS AND STOP CONTROLS — WHICH IS YESTERDAY'S "ORCHESTRATION IS THE NEW SCALING AXIS" AND THE PROPRIOCEPTIVE-DASHBOARD PAPER, BOTH ARRIVING AS SETTINGS ON THE STACK WE ALREADY RUN
bullets.summary: 2.1.269 added `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS`, accepting 1–256, to raise the Workflow tool's per-run concurrent agent limit for inference-bound fan-outs. In the VS Code line it added an agent map: an "N agents" footer pill opens a map of the session's sub-agents with per-agent cards, a Stop agent control, and read-only transcripts, plus live progress rows for running subagents. Two adjacent fixes matter for anyone running scheduled work: cloud routine runs that use subagents were "sometimes being treated as finished too early, which could skip the retry after a real failure or start a duplicate run," and one-off scheduled routines "occasionally running a second time after a transient server error." Also fixed: the git status Claude is told after a compaction is now the CURRENT status rather than the one from the start of the session. Source-quality note: vendor changelog primary; the 256 ceiling is a stated limit, not a benchmarked throughput claim, and no guidance is given on what concurrency is actually useful.
bullets.how: YES, and it is the cheapest of the three bullets to act on. Sep 11 filed OpenAI's Navier-Stokes claim under "agent count under an orchestrator is the new scaling axis; we run one box," and this morning's bullet 3 filed Cursor's delegating coordinator as our own architecture sold back to us. The fan-out half of that is now one environment variable on the stack The Construct already runs — it does not solve the cloud-resident coordinator problem, which remains real and remains the thing Cursor has that we do not, but it does mean the "we run one box" complaint is partly a default we never changed. The agent map is the more interesting one: yesterday's arXiv 2606.30005 argued agents manage their own context better when given a PROPRIOCEPTIVE DASHBOARD, and a per-agent card with a Stop control and a read-only transcript is that idea shipped as UI, for humans first. And the two scheduled-routine fixes are directly load-bearing for this report's own existence — a routine treated as finished too early skips the retry after a real failure, and a one-off routine can run twice after a transient error, which is exactly the class of fault that produces a day with a missing brief or a duplicated one. The compaction/git-status fix is the freshness class again, now on its seventh appearance, and it is worth stating plainly that the vendor keeps finding these in the same place we keep finding ours: what the agent was TOLD about the world, versus what is true now.

bullets.title: TWO SEPTEMBER arXiv PAPERS NAME THE HERMES PROBLEM PROPERLY — "DELEGATION WITHOUT TRUST" ON IDENTITY, AUTHORIZATION AND RUNTIME GOVERNANCE FOR AGENTS HOLDING REAL CREDENTIALS, AND "CONTINUITY" ON SECURITY-CONTEXT CONTRACTS FOR COMPOSABLE AGENT CONTROLS
bullets.summary: arXiv 2609.00267, "Delegation Without Trust: An Empirical Gap Analysis of Identity, Authorization, and Runtime Governance in Multi-Agent LLM Systems," takes as its starting premise that autonomous LLM agents act on a user's behalf WITH CREDENTIALS AND TOOLS, and treats the resulting authorization and governance questions as a distributed-systems problem with measurable gaps rather than a prompt-safety problem. arXiv 2609.05269, "CONTINUITY: Security-Context Contracts for Composable LLM Agent Controls," addresses how controls compose when agents are chained — the case where each link is individually permitted and the composition is not. Adjacent and slightly older but on the same axis: 2603.09619 ("Context Engineering: From Prompts to Corporate Multi-Agent Architecture") proposes five context-quality criteria — relevance, sufficiency, isolation, ECONOMY and PROVENANCE — and 2605.05007 ("Uno-Orchestra: Parsimonious Agent Routing via Selective Delegation") treats delegation cost as the thing to minimize. Source-quality note: arXiv preprints, NOT peer-reviewed, and the two September papers are cited here from listing metadata and abstracts rather than a full read; the 2603 and 2605 papers are from earlier in the year and are included as the framing they supply, not as new news.
bullets.how: MAYBE, because the honest answer is that we do not need a paper to know this, but the vocabulary is worth taking. "Delegation without trust" is a precise four-word description of the open question this morning's bullet 1 ended on: Hermes holds the deploy SSH key, GSC and GitHub write access, and its `.env` contains a live `OPENROUTER_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` line, so context delegated to that path leaves the building. That is not a breach and it was correctly not called one. It is an AUTHORIZATION AND RUNTIME GOVERNANCE gap, and it now has a literature name and, per 2609.05269, a compositional form — Cowork delegates to Hermes, Hermes delegates to a fallback route, and no single link is individually wrong. The genuinely useful steal is 2603.09619's five criteria, because two of them are the exact two columns bullet 1 just re-scoped: ECONOMY and PROVENANCE. When standing action (a)'s schema gets written, those five criteria are a better spine than the eight fields this report has accreted one fire at a time, and the eighth field proposed this morning (what channel verified a payment-adjacent action) is a special case of provenance. The reason this is MAYBE and not YES is that nothing here changes what to do tomorrow; it changes what to call it, which matters only at the point somebody writes the file.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS — (c) IS RE-SCOPED RATHER THAN ADVANCED, AND THE RE-SCOPE IS THE DAY'S REAL OUTPUT; (b) AND (e) WERE DUE TODAY AND ARE NOW DUE-AND-UNDONE; (a) IS TWO DAYS OVERDUE AND HAS GAINED A BETTER SPINE THAN THE ONE IT HAD
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's open decisions, re-verified this fire. (a) MISALIGNMENT / MCP INCIDENT LOG — TWO DAYS OVERDUE, eight fields accreted, and bullet 4 offers to replace the accretion with five named criteria (relevance, sufficiency, isolation, economy, provenance) from 2603.09619; the eighth field is a special case of the fifth. (b) ENTRA'S FOUR MCP CONTROLS AS A CONFIG SCRIPT — WAS DUE TODAY, still five lines, still unwritten as of this fire. (c) SKILL-CORPUS AUDIT — RE-SCOPED TODAY, and this is the only item that moved: it is no longer one overdue artifact but three columns with three different costs — ECONOMY is `/skill-doctor`, one command; PROVENANCE is a find plus `git log -1` across the twelve third-party repos Sep 11 enumerated, and is sold by nobody; QUALITY at corpus scale is not a product and should be scoped down to the skills `/skill-doctor` shows actually running. (e) CADENCE-COST MEASUREMENT — WAS DUE TODAY, one number, unwritten, and the Sep 14 limit change is now two days out. UNSET LEVERS: `maxEffortLevel` and `--system-prompt-snapshot off`, unchanged for a fourth day, plus a new one from bullet 3 — `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS`, currently at its default.
bullets.how: YES, and the count needs stating without decoration. Ten fires. Two items were due today and neither was done. (a) is two days late, (e) is now late with a deadline behind it. What this fire produced is not a closed item; it is a CORRECTION that makes one item smaller and honest, and a correction is worth more than another restatement — Sep 11 concluded (c) was "build-or-buy, priced," and that was wrong in the column that mattered, which would have sent whoever finally sat down to do it shopping for a product that does not exist. The one thing worth carrying forward is the proportion from Sep 11 that held again today: the work that gets done is the work small enough to do inside the fire that found it. Bullet 1's correction cost one lookup. (b) is five lines and (e) is one number, and they have now been described more times than they would have taken to write.

praxis_lesson: THE OPEN-THE-PRIMARY RULE WAS WRITTEN FOR COMPANIES AND IT APPLIES JUST AS HARD TO TOOLS AND TO OUR OWN BACKLOG ITEMS. Sep 11's lesson was that an aggregator is a pointer and never a source, learned by getting AIR's raise, country, founders and product wrong. Today the same failure was available in a different costume: `claude plugin eval` shipped overnight, it is described as scored reproducible plugin evaluation, and the lazy report files it as "standing action (c), shipped" — the fourth consecutive fire to announce that our overdue audit is now purchasable. Opening the reference inverted it. `plugin eval` is an AUTHOR's harness that tests one plugin against tests you wrote; `/skill-doctor` is a usage-and-cost report that says nothing about provenance or quality. The audit is not buyable in its most important column, and four fires of "build-or-buy, priced" were describing a market that does not exist for the thing we actually need. THE RULE THIS FIRE EARNS: A CAPABILITY CLAIM ABOUT A TOOL IS A DESCRIPTION UNTIL YOU READ WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES — and the most dangerous descriptions are the ones that flatter your backlog by telling you somebody else already solved it. Note which direction the error ran. Sep 10's error was under-reading a story; Sep 11's was over-reading a name; today's available error was RELIEF — the pleasant conclusion that an overdue task had been handled by the vendor. Relief is the tell. The second lesson is smaller and it is about this report's own conduct: this morning's fire wrote a threat-report bullet that made a supported configuration (a third-party `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) sound like a finding, and a changelog line from two days earlier shows Anthropic treats breaking those endpoints as a regression worth fixing. The verdict was right and the tone was slightly wrong, and tone is what survives into next month's memory. When the correction is available the same day, take it.
